I’ve farmed these 10 mu here in Quzhou for 20 years. I’m 44, finished junior high. I went to a training meeting once that the township put on, and I talk to the fertilizer dealer when I buy, but honestly I do what I’ve always done and I watch the neighbors who get good yields.

My 8 mu of wheat-maize is my main income. I plant improved wheat seed — not the old traditional kind, the kind from the seed station that my neighbor tried first and got good results. Last October I rotary tilled after the maize and sowed wheat. For base fertilizer I put 30 kg of compound fertilizer per mu — 15-15-15, the kind in the 40 kg bags. Then in spring I topdressed urea twice: 20 kg per mu at green-up, 15 kg per mu at jointing. That’s about 20 kg nitrogen total per mu. I irrigate three times from the well: green-up water, jointing water, and grain-filling water. I spray three times — herbicide once, then insecticide and fungicide later if the weather turns humid. I expect about 560 kg per mu this year if no disaster hits.

For summer maize, I sow hybrid seed right after wheat harvest in June. I do no-tillage now — just clear the wheat stubble and plant directly. Saves fuel and time. I put 25 kg per mu of compound fertilizer in the seed row, then at big trumpet I spread another 25 kg per mu of urea. That’s about 18 kg nitrogen. I irrigate twice, and spray twice: herbicide at sowing, then insecticide if I see worms. I expect 680 kg per mu.

My other 2.1 mu is cotton. I plough deep for cotton in April — cotton roots need soft soil. I use improved cotton seed. Base fertilizer is 35 kg compound per mu, then I add urea at flowering. Total about 18 kg nitrogen, 6 kg phosphorus, 10 kg potassium. Cotton drinks more water than people think — I irrigate three times. And it needs four pesticide sprays, no way around it, the bollworms come every year. I expect 260 kg per mu of seed cotton.

I worry about money. My husband and older son work off-farm, so we have some cash, but fertilizer is expensive. A bag of urea is over 100 yuan now. Still, I learned: skimp on fertilizer and you lose everything. Better to put one extra bag per mu than to have yellow wheat. I do basically what I did last year. Last year was fine, the well had water, so I’m not changing anything big. I watch Lao Wang’s field across the road — if he sprays, I spray. If his wheat looks darker than mine, I add a bit more urea next time.
